angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,156,253 km at 78.73 pc = 0.2 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.7014 +/- 0.0193 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 78.73 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.662 +/- 0.071 solar radii from Kroft et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-6054.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..150K/abstract): 1,156,253 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.107 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Kroft et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-6054.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..150K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6047 +/- 50 K from Kroft et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6054.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..150K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Kroft et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-6054.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..150K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-6054.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.041, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
